messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 429s observed on /v1/generate (pool=hotpath-us-east-1). 5m 429 rate=18%. Queue depth rising from ~200 -> ~1.2k. Triggered: pool exhausted + autoscaler AcquireTimeouts. Paging oncall.

oncall-alex: i'm paged, grabbing pager and joining. what region/tenant impact?

sre-john: joining. initial glance: hotpath pool at 98% GPU util, autoscaler logged repeated AcquireTimeouts to cloud provider. also seeing token-bucket rejections on the realtime tier. hypothesis: combined conservative token refill + strict tier throughput prevented short bursts during capacity pressure.

infra-nina: autoscale logs (excerpt):
```
2026-03-15T17:02:05Z autoscaler: AcquireTimeout for request pool=hotpath-us-east-1 attempt=3
2026-03-15T17:02:12Z autoscaler: backoff applied cooldown=300s
2026-03-15T17:02:45Z policy: tier realtime throughput_cap=120rps burst_refill=2.5
```

eng-ryan: pulling metrics ->
```
# metrics snapshot
gpu.hotpool.utilization{pool=hotpath-us-east-1} = 0.98
requests.queue.size = 1240
http.429.rate /v1/generate = 0.182
autoscale.acquire_timeouts = 37
```

oncall-alex: pm/eng: are high-value customers affected? need to triage comms.

pm-elaine: support reports errors from 3 enterprise customers: billing-prod, chatflow, search-corp. Not global, but their critical paths are failing. I'm preparing an outbound.

sre-john: mitigation plan (short): 1) relax token-bucket refill for realtime tier to allow bursts 2) temporarily increase throughput cap for hotpath 3) emergency autoscale bypass (allow +2 GPUs, bypass cooldown). executing now: step 1.

infra-nina: applying patch to policy service: `burst_refill: 2.5 -> 8.0` for tier=realtime. Rolling config.

eng-ryan: rolling update triggered. policy service logs: 
```
2026-03-15T17:03:12Z POLICY reload ok
2026-03-15T17:03:14Z tokenbucket realtime refill=8.0
```

support: outbound draft sent to affected customers: "we are aware of elevated errors for generate endpoints, mitigation underway, ETA ~10m". sent to billing-prod + chatflow; they acked.

sre-john: immediate effect: 429s dropped from 18% -> ~9% within 60s. queue trending down from 1.2k -> 650. still monitoring.

oncall-alex: infra-nina, please trigger emergency scale up while we monitor refill change.

infra-nina: triggering cloud scale-up +2 gpus for hotpath pool, request accepted, provisioning ETA ~90s.

incident-bot: CLOUD: Provisioning accepted for 2 instances (provider-id: aws-i-abc123), eta=95s.

eng-ryan: adding precautionary routing: overflow->us-west for realtime tier if queue > 500 for >60s. updating routing rules now.

pm-elaine: notifying customers with ETA updates. asking support to confirm when errors drop below threshold.

support: confirmed: billing-prod reports reduced errors. chatflow still seeing intermittent failures but improved.

sre-john: new numbers: queue=480, http.429=4.3%, autoscale add completed (+2 GPUs). Recommend keep burst_refill=8.0 and throughput_cap increased for 30m, then evaluate. Need a postmortem to decide permanent changes.

oncall-alex: i'll open a PD incident and assign postmortem owners: infra-nina (autoscaler/cloud), eng-ryan (policy/routing), pm-elaine (customer comms).

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Severity=Sev2 -> mitigated. Summary: resource exhaustion on hotpath pool + autoscaler acquire timeouts under burst load; token-bucket/burst_refill and tier throughput caps prevented graceful handling of short spikes. Mitigation: increased burst_refill, temporary throughput cap raise, emergency autoscale bypass, cross-region overflow.

sre-john: suggested long-term actions: - automated smoke test to validate autoscaler under synthetic burst - alert tuning so tokenbucket breaches create proactive autoscale attempts - make burst_refill correlated with pool capacity/reserved headroom - document rollback plan for burst_refill changes

pm-elaine: legal/compliance wants list of impacted tenants and exact error windows for SLA. support will provide.

support: will attach tenant list + timestamps to PD ticket within 30m.

oncall-alex: closing pager in 10m if stable. great work team :thumbsup:
